title: 闻官军收河南河北
titleEn: Hearing That the Imperial Army Has Retaken Henan and Hebei
author: 杜甫
intro: After eight years of civil war, the news finally comes: the rebels are beaten. Du Fu weeps, laughs, throws his books together and plans the whole journey home in one breath — often called the happiest poem he ever wrote.
analysis: 这首诗被称为杜甫“生平第一首快诗”。安史之乱打了七八年，杜甫流落在四川，忽然听说官军收复了叛军的老巢河南、河北。第一、二句写刚听到消息：一下子泪流满面，衣服都湿了——这是喜极而泣（高兴到哭）。第三、四句写家人：回头看妻子和孩子，脸上的愁容早没了；自己胡乱卷起书本，高兴得快要发狂。第五、六句写打算：大白天也要放声唱歌、尽情喝酒，趁着春光正好，和家人一起回故乡。最后两句写回家的路线：从巴峡穿过巫峡，再到襄阳，再奔洛阳，四个地名一口气连下来，好像人已经在船上飞奔。全诗节奏越来越快，把狂喜写得淋漓尽致（非常充分）。
analysisEn: Critics have called this Du Fu's happiest poem. The An Lushan Rebellion had dragged on for nearly eight years, and Du Fu was stranded in Sichuan, far from home, when word came that government troops had retaken the rebels' heartland north of the Yellow River. The first couplet is the moment the news arrives: he bursts into tears and his clothes are soaked — tears of joy, not grief. In the second he turns to his family. His wife and children no longer look worried at all, and he starts rolling up his books any old way, almost mad with happiness. The third couplet is about celebration and plans: sing out loud in broad daylight, drink as much as you like, and travel home with the green spring for company. The last couplet is the route itself — through the Ba Gorge, through the Wu Gorge, down to Xiangyang, on to Luoyang. Four place names in one breath, as if the boat were already racing downstream. The rhythm speeds up line by line, and the reader is swept along with his excitement. (In fact, the journey home would never happen.)
background: Du Fu (712–770) wrote this in spring 763 in Zizhou (today's Santai, Sichuan), when the last rebel leaders were defeated and the An Lushan Rebellion finally ended. He longed to return to Luoyang, where his family came from, but he died seven years later without getting there.
pronunciation: 衣裳 cháng（统编教材注 cháng，古音；现代汉语“衣裳”读 yī shang）；却看 kàn；妻子 qī zǐ（妻子和儿女，不是现代的“妻子 qī zi”）；还乡 huán；蓟 jì；涕 tì；漫卷 màn juǎn。
version: 采用通行教材版本，各本基本一致，无重要异文。原诗题下有杜甫自注：“余田园在东京”（东京指洛阳）。

lines.py: jiàn wài hū chuán shōu jì běi
lines.lit: Beyond Jiange, suddenly news: Jibei is taken back;
lines.en: Here beyond the Sword Pass, sudden news: the north is ours again!

lines.py: chū wén tì lèi mǎn yī cháng
lines.lit: first hearing it, tears fill my clothes.
lines.en: At the first word of it, tears soak my clothes.

lines.py: què kàn qī zǐ chóu hé zài
lines.lit: Turning to look at wife and children — where is their sorrow?
lines.en: I turn to my wife and children: where has all the worry gone?

lines.py: màn juǎn shī shū xǐ yù kuáng
lines.lit: Carelessly rolling up poems and books, joyful almost to madness.
lines.en: I sweep my books together, wild with joy.

lines.py: bái rì fàng gē xū zòng jiǔ
lines.lit: In broad day, singing aloud, I must drink freely;
lines.en: In broad daylight I'll sing at the top of my voice and drink my fill,

lines.py: qīng chūn zuò bàn hǎo huán xiāng
lines.lit: green spring as companion, a fine time to return home.
lines.en: and with the green spring beside us, we'll head for home.

lines.py: jí cóng bā xiá chuān wū xiá
lines.lit: At once from Ba Gorge through Wu Gorge;
lines.en: Straight from the Ba Gorge, on through the Wu Gorge,

lines.py: biàn xià xiāng yáng xiàng luò yáng
lines.lit: then down to Xiangyang, toward Luoyang.
lines.en: then down to Xiangyang — and on to Luoyang!

words.note: 古义是听见，“新闻”还保留这个意思；现代汉语“闻”多指用鼻子闻。
朝廷的军队，和“叛军”相对。

words.en: beyond Jiange (the Sword Pass), i.e. Sichuan
words.note: 剑门关以南，指四川一带，当时杜甫在这里。
今河北北部，是叛军的老巢。
“涕”古义是眼泪，现代汉语“鼻涕”指鼻子流出的东西。
“却”这里是“回过头”；现代汉语“却”是“但是”。
古义是妻子和儿女两种人；现代汉语“妻子 qīzi”只指老婆。古今异义的典型例子。
“漫”是随便，“卷”是卷起（古代的书是卷轴）。
“欲”是“快要”；现代汉语说“欣喜若狂”。
放声歌唱；现代汉语也说“放声高歌”。
“纵”是放开、不控制，现代汉语有“放纵”“纵情”。
古义指春天的美景；现代汉语“青春”指年轻的时候。
“还”读 huán，是“回”；成语有“衣锦还乡”。
长江上游的峡谷；巫峡是今天“长江三峡”之一。
今湖北襄阳、河南洛阳，两个城市名今天还在用。

imagery.name: 泪
imagery.zh: 这里的泪不是悲伤，而是喜极而泣，压抑多年的苦一下子化成了泪水。
imagery.en: Not tears of grief but of joy — years of pent-up suffering released all at once.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 放开喝酒是庆祝，写出诗人狂喜、想要尽情发泄的心情。
imagery.en: Drinking freely is pure celebration — the poet letting go after years of strain.
